INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE JULY 14, 2021 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

The Planning Commission meeting will be closed to the public in compliance with
Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus.
Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via teleconference with members participating
remotely. Considering this, the customary meeting format has been modified. Even with
this change in format, the City is still encouraging public participation and wishes to make
residents aware of the following opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org.
  They will be shared with the Commission Members prior to the meeting and will be
  made part of the permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before
  7:00 p.m. the day before the meeting. Please be advised that public comments
  submitted by emails or any other format to the City are public records that
  will be made available for public viewing.

  3) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may
  email planning@cityoflaverne.org by 6:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting with a
  phone number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the
  appropriate time during the meeting for your comment.

  4) Additionally, if you wish to participate via Zoom, you will need to register before
  5:00 p.m. on the date of the meeting and please be aware that space is limited.

  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_nRu4IRPgR8GGzeur5Tps-w

  You will be provided a link after registering and will have the ability to watch the
  meeting live. If you wish to speak during the meeting, you can “raise your hand” as
  appropriate on the current agenda item(s). Once it is your turn to speak, you will be
  brought into the meeting and have the ability to speak and turn on your video when
  called upon.

public records that will be made available for public viewing. Regular Meetings are held on the 2
Wednesday of every month. In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability
who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City
Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

Materials related to an item on this agenda, submitted to the Planning Commission after distribution of the

CITY OF LA VERNE
Community Development Department

DATE:  July 14, 2021

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Gabriel Rivera, Assistant Planner

SUBJECT:  Case No. 53-21CUP; an amendment to an existing Conditional Use Permit to allow
  for the expansion of La Verne Brewing Company and associated alcohol services
  at 2125 Wright Avenue Suites C12-13

AGENDA SUMMARY

On May 10, 2021, the applicant Thomas Tredennick, owner of La Verne Brewing Company, has
submitted an application to amend the La Verne Brewing Company’s existing Conditional Use
Permit for the operation of a small-scale microbrewery to include the adjacent location, along with
a front and rear patio, and operating hour changes at 2125 Wright Avenue, Suite C12-13, in the
La Verne Business Park center. The brewery is located in the Business Park sector, which is
located within the boundaries of the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan (SP86-12). On-site and off-site
sale of alcoholic beverages are regulated by the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan, as well as Chapter
18.80 of the La Verne Municipal Code, both of which require a Conditional Use Permit.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff and the Development Review Committee recommend Planning Commission approval of
Resolution No.1276, which approves Case No. 53-21CUP, based on the findings and subject to
the conditions of approval.

BACKGROUND

The commercial space at 2125 Wright Avenue, Suite C12-13, in the La Verne Business Park
Center currently is occupied by a bike shop (Crazy Bear Bikes). In 2012, the applicants filed for
a Conditional Use Permit (40-12CUP) to operate a microbrewery with retail sales at 2125 Wright
Avenue, Suites C14-15. Planning Commission approved the proposal on June 6, 2012 under
Resolution No. 1075. The following year, in 2013, the applicants filed to amend their Conditional
Use Permit to allow the applicants to extend their operating hours from 6:00am-11:00pm, which
was approved by the Planning Commission under Resolution No.1122 on October 9, 2013.
Prior to the amendment, the applicants were only allowed to operate from 6:00am-9:00pm. The
Arrow Corridor Specific Plan allows for a wineries, breweries, or distilleries with a Conditional
Use Permit in the Business Park sector.

The applicants are proposing to expand their existing Conditional Use Permit for the operation
of a small-scale microbrewery to include the neighboring suites, Suites C12-13, along with the
proposed front patio and rear patio. The public notice that was sent out for this hearing indicated
that the applicant was also proposing to extend their operating hours from 6:00am-11:00pm to
 PC Agenda Report
Case No. 53-21CUP
July 14, 2021
Page 2

6:00am-2:00am, but staff has since worked with the applicant to reduce the proposed operating
hours to 6:00am-12:00am. Both staff and the Police Department support this change in
operating hours. Staff did receive a public comment regarding the original proposed operating
hours, as shown on Attachment F, but the new proposed changes would address this public
comment.

SITE PLAN REVIEW

Location – The applicant requests approval of a Conditional Use Permit amendment to expand
the size of the current brewery to include the neighboring tenant space, C12-13, which measures
3,456 square feet within the La Verne Business Park center. The applicants have leased the
tenant space and have opted to share a portion of the tenant space with Crazy Bear Bikes as
shown on attachment C. Crazy Bear Bikes will occupy 816 square feet of the frontal portion of the
warehouse within C12-13, while also utilizing both office spaces at the front of C12-13. The bike
shop had received a Certificate of Use and Occupancy in February 2021 for the utilization of C12,
but the new layout that is being proposed by the applicants is not what was originally approved
under the Certificate of Use and Occupancy. Due to this, staff has placed a condition for the
applicant to obtain a new Certificate of Use and Occupancy in order to update the layout of the
tenant space. The applicants will be utilizing the back portion of suites C12-13, which will comprise
of a 2364.18 square foot game and serving area. The bike shop will be screened off from the
serving and games area, but the restrooms will remain accessible by both the bike shop and the
microbrewery. The bike shop portion of the space will have an occupancy load of 23 persons,
while the portion utilized by the applicants will have an occupancy load of 158 persons.

In addition to expanding into Suite C12-13, the applicants are also proposing a permanent 2,640
square foot back patio, which will connect tenant spaces C15-14 and C12-13 as shown on
Attachment B. The rear patio will measure 30 feet in length by 98 feet in width. The Fire
Department requires that there is a minimum of 26 foot drive aisle clearance between the
proposed patio and the parking spaces on the opposite side. With the proposed rear patio, the
drive aisle would be 31 feet, which does satisfy the requirements set by the Fire Department. The
applicants are also proposing a semi-permanent front patio that will be a total of 1,296 square
feet. The front patio will measure 18 feet in length and 72 feet in width. The proposed front patio
will occupy a total of 11 parking spaces. A portion of the front patio that occupied the parking
spaces in front of Suites C14-15 was originally temporarily approved by the City under the COVID-
19 Outdoor Dining program and through ABC during the COVID-19 pandemic. The applicants are
proposing to use the semi-permanent front patio from March 1 to September 1. The originally
approved front patio portion will be extended so it connects Suites C15-12 as shown on
Attachment C. The occupancy load for the proposed rear patio would support 176 persons, while
the front patio has an occupancy load of 86.

Parking – The La Verne Business Park Center currently has 135 total confirmed spaces provided
with an excess of 56.1 spaces. With the new expansion of the brewery, combined with the bike
shop use, and outdoor patio areas, the total spaces required for the center would be 138.42. Staff
has reviewed the parking requirements for the La Verne Business Park center. While the Arrow
Corridor Specific Plan is not clear when there are non-industrial uses and what type of parking
requirements the use requires, staff has applied a restaurant parking ratio of 1:100 sq. ft. for
Gene’s Grinders, as well as the full brewery space in Suites C14/15. Suites C12/13 would retain
a parking ratio of 1:500, since the space us utilized by both the bike shop and as extra assembly
space for the brewery when needed. In that analysis there is a parking deficit of 3.4 spaces,
 PC Agenda Report
Case No. 53-21CUP
July 14, 2021
Page 3

however, the operating hours of the brewery are opposite to the operating hours of most of the
surrounding uses in the center. For example, Gene’s Grinders operates from 7:00AM-2:30PM,
while La Verne Brewing Company opens to the public from 3:00PM to the proposed 12:00am
time. Therefore, there would not be a significant impact on parking and the brewery would have
sufficient parking access.

ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW

There are no proposed changes to the exterior of the existing building.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES

The sale and consumption of alcohol will be conducted within Suites C12-15, the rear patio, and
front patio. On-site alcohol sales will not have a negative impact on surrounding uses as long as
the conditions of the existing Conditional Use Permit are adhered to. Neither staff nor the Police
Department has had any issues with the selling of alcohol at the current business since it opened
in 2012.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The application is Categorically Exempt (15061 (b) (3)) under the provisions of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the La Verne Environmental Guidelines. No additional
environmental review is required.

CITY OF LA VERNE
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE
  Wednesday, July 14, 2021

1.  Chairperson Jason Simison called the regular meeting of the La Verne Planning
  Commission to order at 6:30 p.m. He stated that all comments should be sent to
  planning@cityoflaverne.org.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chairperson Simison led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL: Planning Commissioners present: Jeff Allred, Thomas Allison,
  and Jason Simison. Not present: Jason Lorge and Phil May. Advisory personnel
  present: Community Development Director Eric Scherer, City Attorney Bob
  Kress, Assistant Planner Gabriel Rivera and Secretary Natalie Hiatt.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  No public comments were received.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  May 12, 2021

  It was moved by Commissioner Allred and seconded by Commissioner Allison to
  approve the minutes. Motion carried by a 2-0 vote (Chairperson Simison
  abstained).

PUBLIC HEARINGS

6.  CASE NO. 53-21CUP – AN AMMENDMENT TO AN EXISTING
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT TO ALLOW FOR THE EXPANSION OF
  LA VERNE BREWING COMPANY AND ASSOCIATED ALCOHOL
  SERVICES AT 2125 WRIGHT AVENUE SUITES C12-13.

  RESOLUTION NO. 1276

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  AMMENDING THE CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT FOR THE
 Planning Commission Minutes
July 14, 2021
  OPERATION OF A SMALL SCALE MICROBREWERY AT 2125
  WRIGHT AVENUE SUITE C12-C15 (CASE NO. 53-21CUP), AND
  AFFIRMING THAT THIS APPLICATION IS CATEGORICALLY
  EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY
  ACT.

  Assistant Planner Gabriel Rivera presented his report.

  Chairperson Simison opened the public hearing.

  La Verne Brewery General Manager Ken Maxey was present at the meeting. Mr.
  Maxey thanked staff for their help.

  Chairperson Simison closed the public hearing.

  The Commissioners proceeded to ask questions regarding parking, the patio
  extension, live entertainment, and the impact on neighboring businesses.

  Commissioner Allred asked for a modification to Condition 26 regarding exterior
  advertising.

  It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner Allred to
  approve Case No. 53-21CUP with the modification to Condition No. 26 in the
  resolution. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

OTHER MATTERS/INFORMATION

7.  FUTURE MEETING LOGISTICS DISCUSSION

  Mr. Scherer stated that the City Manager and City Council is working to hold a
  hybrid meeting that allows for an in-person and virtual for the August 2nd
  meeting. Mr. Scherer expects that the September Planning Commission meeting
  will be held in-person only.

  COMMISSIONER UPDATE/ NEW STAFF

  Mr. Scherer announced that Commissioner May has resigned from Planning
  Commission effective immediately. Commissioner May recently retired and
  decided that he could not make the time commitment needed to fulfill his term.
  Applications for a new Planning Commissioner will open July 22nd through
  August 12th. The new Commissioner will fill the unexpired term and will be
  eligible for reappointment for two four year terms.

  The Commissioners thanked Phil May for his service and congratulated him on
  his retirement.

July 14, 2021
  Mr. Scherer announced a new staff member was recently hired. Assistant Planner
  Parker Stringfellow will be formally introduced at the next Planning Commission
  meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:03p.m. The next regular meeting of the Planning
  Commission will be held August 11, 2021 at 6:30 p.m.
